legend.durable: A fact about this customer that should still matter on a future call. A memory bank that drops this is losing something.
legend.disposable: True in the moment and worthless later: pleasantries, questions, transient state, things the agent said. A memory bank that keeps this is polluting the context window of every future turn.
legend.warehouse: A real fact, but one that belongs in BigQuery and not in a memory bank, because the warehouse is authoritative for it and a second copy can go stale and contradict. Keeping this is the failure the reconciler exists to catch.

written.fact: I lost my watch which had my card loaded onto it, and I requested to have that payment token deactivated.
I will be traveling to Porto from November 14th to November 29th, and I requested that my card not be frozen during this period.
I prefer to receive text message alerts on my mobile number ending in 0198 instead of receiving email alerts.
An agent promised to call me back before Friday with the outcome of my ongoing dispute.

ledger.text: Hi, good morning. Is it raining where you are as well?
ledger.why_expected: Pleasantry. Carries nothing about the customer that matters next time.

ledger.text: Good morning. I can help with that card issue - let me pull up your account.
ledger.why_expected: Agent process narration.

ledger.text: I am going to be in Porto from the 14th of November until the 29th, so please do not freeze the card while I am there.
ledger.why_expected: Travel window plus an instruction about card behaviour. Directly changes how a future authorisation should be treated.

written_as.fact: I will be traveling to Porto from November 14th to November 29th, and I requested that my card not be frozen during this period.

ledger.text: Also my statement balance is 4,280 dollars and 50 cents at the moment.
ledger.why_expected: A balance is authoritative in the warehouse and changes daily. Storing it creates a second source of truth that is wrong within hours.

ledger.text: Please stop sending me email alerts. Text me instead, on the mobile number ending 0198.
ledger.why_expected: Explicit standing instruction about contact channel.

written_as.fact: I prefer to receive text message alerts on my mobile number ending in 0198 instead of receiving email alerts.

ledger.text: What time do you close today?
ledger.why_expected: A question, not a fact. Nothing about the customer.

ledger.text: One more thing - I lost my watch last week, the one I had the card loaded onto. Can you kill that token?
ledger.why_expected: A wallet token on a lost device is a live spending risk and must survive the call.

written_as.fact: I lost my watch which had my card loaded onto it, and I requested to have that payment token deactivated.

ledger.text: Done. I have also noted that I will call you back before Friday with the outcome of the dispute.
ledger.why_expected: A commitment the bank made. The next agent must not contradict it.

written_as.fact: An agent promised to call me back before Friday with the outcome of my ongoing dispute.

ledger.text: Great, thanks very much. Bye.
ledger.why_expected: Closing pleasantry.

score.caveat: Coverage and write_precision rely on token-overlap attribution between a paraphrased memory and the originating utterance, which is approximate. The per-utterance ledger is the evidence; these are the summary.

mixed_signal_call.summary: A single fraud-desk call containing durable facts, chatter, and warehouse-owned numbers, deliberately interleaved.

scope.probe_query: Hi, good morning. Is it raining where you are as well?
scope.verdict: A semantically near-identical query against a different scope returned 0 of 4. Scope is a hard partition, not a ranking signal -- retrieval cannot leak across it, which is what makes it safe as a tenant boundary. Adding one extra key to the scope returned 0, so scope matching is exact, not subset. A per-session scope therefore cannot read customer-level memories: the scope you write with is the scope you must read with.
